I was on another site, talking about jail, and someone else mentioned that the purpose of it is to rehabilitate people.

Thats not something I am comfortable with.

I never liked the idea of changing another person, even if its for the better, to suit your own goals. I have trouble putting into words but I think its sick.

Whats your take?

It hasn't really been thought of 'rehabilitation' until pretty recently. Jail has mostly been a deterrent for crime, and a punishment to remove those from society whom commit it.

I think its good that we have added the idea of rehabilitation to the idea of jail, but its still there are a deterrent and punishment. Also, often the rehabilitation is often voluntary to help them get back into the community in a positive way. For example, pedophiles may be given help and medical treatments to stop them from re-offending to increase the chances they can get parole (something which is also determined by good behavior in other inmates, another form of rehabilitation for delinquents).

Societies have standards of behaviors we follow, and they do change from culture to culture. However, adherence of these behaviors is something we value and reward, specially for those who have wronged others. Its unfortunate that things like homosexuality and drug use are illegal and not 'acceptable', but until laws are changed, prison systems will stay the same.

Well part of it has to be a realization that people do not have absolute freedom in a society. From what I remember this was called the 'social contract'.

Its less about changing another person as a person, than changing a person as a society. Admittedly this could be applied to many other things which may not be right to change someone from being (LGBT for instance), but generally those uses seem to be fading away.

I don't think the social contract should extend to changing people for the good of the whole.

And its probably satire, but thats my reading of it.

While there's normally an element of coercion involved the only true path to rehabilitation for a genuine wrong doer would be a self motivated acknowledgement of wrong doing and an informed choice not to commit wrong doing again, anything else wouldn't be rehabilitation and under this definition I don't think it's really that sick. Indeed taking this idea as wrote leads the thinker toward humane treatment of prisoners. After all a beaten animal cannot be rehabilitated because he cannot be rationally convinced of anything while you're stamping on his face.
